paragraphs.text: Many schools now ask children to type most of their work, and some educators have proposed dropping handwriting lessons altogether. I think this would be a mistake, although not for the reasons usually given.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: The romantic argument, that handwriting is a beautiful art that must be preserved, does not persuade me. Plenty of beautiful skills have disappeared without great loss. The stronger argument is practical: studies suggest that children who write letters by hand learn to recognise them more quickly than those who only type.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: At the same time, it seems pointless to spend hours on joined-up writing. Neat, readable print is enough for almost every purpose in adult life, and the time saved could be given to typing, which children will certainly need.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Examinations present a further problem. As long as many national exams are written by hand, pupils who rarely hold a pen will be at a disadvantage, and it is unfair to test them in a way they have not practised.
paragraphs.label: D

items.prompt: The writer supports the proposal to stop teaching handwriting.
The writer is persuaded by the argument that handwriting is an art worth preserving.
The writer thinks children should be taught to type.
The writer believes most teachers prefer marking handwritten work.
The writer considers it unfair to make pupils write exams by hand if they rarely practise handwriting.
